issues.passage: At the zenith of the dig, crews finally exposed the lowest foundation stones of the fort.
issues.why: "At the zenith of the dig" is valid figurative use: zenith = peak/high point of the excavation project (when the key discovery was made). "Lowest foundation stones" names depth in the ground, not the opposite of zenith; a careful reader would accept the sentence as correct.

fix.correctPassage: The empire reached its zenith under the second emperor’s long and stable rule.
wrongPassages: The firm reached its zenith the year losses forced a major restructuring of the company.
After the scandal, the senator’s career sank to its zenith and never recovered public trust.
Historians place the movement’s zenith in the obscure years before it gained any public following.
